exposure: Delayed pushing protocol (2 hours vs 3 hours)
outcome: Mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal delivery, instrumental vaginal delivery, Caesarean section)
Neonatal morbidity (5-minute Apgar score, umbilical cord pH, transfer to NICU)
cohort: Low-risk nulliparous women with a term singleton fetus in cephalic presentation, who received epidural analgesia and reached full dilation with a normal fetal heart rate
finding: Women in the group with a protocol allowing delayed pushing for up to 3 hours had a significantly lower risk of instrumental vaginal delivery compared to the group with a protocol allowing up to 2 hours of delayed pushing, with no difference in Caesarean section rates or maternal/neonatal morbidity.
